subject.title: [Feature]: Track data provenance across session boundaries for persistent state

question: What durable provenance contract should OpenClaw expose for tool-derived state that may influence future sessions?
rationale: The issue defines security-sensitive public Plugin SDK hooks, persisted state metadata, and read-time trust policy; automation cannot choose that boundary safely without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design the provenance contract first
options.body: Approve a small architecture/design pass that chooses the host-authored provenance fields, durable write/read hook shape, memory schema impact, and plugin policy boundary before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to memory-only tagging
options.body: Treat this as a memory-plugin feature first, accepting that files, config, scheduled tasks, and other durable writes remain outside the initial provenance model.

options.title: Defer to the broader tainting effort
options.body: Keep this issue as supporting context and make the broader security tainting proposal the implementation driver.

recommendation.title: Design the provenance contract first
recommendation.body: Approve a small architecture/design pass that chooses the host-authored provenance fields, durable write/read hook shape, memory schema impact, and plugin policy boundary before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The most immediate unresolved boundary is the plugin hook contract and host-provided policy surface, where this person has the strongest recent history signal.
